source: Wu and Yang (2022), CLeaR, PMLR 177:904-926; Table 1, printed p.11; Section 6.1.1 (Simulation I)
design: RCT: X~U[-1,1], U~N(0,1), A~Bernoulli(0.5). OS: A~Bernoulli(0.5), (X,U)|A ~ N(0, [[1, A-0.5], [A-0.5, 1]]). Y = 1 + X + 0.5X^2 + U + A*tau(X) + 0.5*eps, tau = 1 + 2X + 0.75X^2, confounding function c(X) = X.
metric: RMSE: per replicate sqrt(mean_test (tau_hat - tau)^2), averaged over replicates
methods: rct oa; os oa; int oa; rct rlearner; os rlearner; int rlearner; rct rf; os rf; KPS lasso; KPS linear; naive rlearner
benchmark_gap_or_overrides: Set n_obs=2000, n_rct_train in {200, 500, 1000} and n_eval=100000.
benchmark_method_mapping: int rlearner -> integrative_r_quadratic (degree-2 basis, SCAD); other columns have no matching recipe
notes: 1) The released README labels Simulations I and II in reverse; the benchmark follows the paper. 2) In this branch gen_data returns tau = 0 (true_tau_coef is built but not returned), so RMSE against the returned tau would be wrong; the true CATE is 1 + 2x + cf*x^2, and cf defaults to 0 in the signature while the paper uses 0.75. 3) The driver that produced Tables 1 and 2 is not released. 4) OS-only columns are printed once, in the n=500 row, and apply to every n. 5) Per the README, the rct/os/naive R-learners use the L1 rlasso while int rlearner uses SCAD, so their regularizers differ. 6) A replay of the released code over 100 seeds (replay_intr_tables) agrees with 9 of the 10 R-learner values, including all three int rlearner values; naive rlearner at n=1000 gives 0.490 against 0.50. The benchmark translation agrees with the released code at every n (int rlearner 0.234, 0.134 and 0.088).

source: Wu and Yang (2022), CLeaR, PMLR 177:904-926; Table 2, printed p.11; Section 6.1.2 (Simulation II)
design: Population 1e5, X~N(0,I_10), X10 unobserved. Y(a) = X1 + X10 + a*tau(W) + eps(a), eps~N(0,1), tau = 1 + sum_{j<=J} X_j. RCT selection logit = -7 - X1 + X2; RCT propensity logit = -1 - X1 + X2. OS: 500 units sampled from the population, propensity logit = -1 - X1 + X2 + b*X10.
evaluation: All 1e5 population units (includes RCT and OS units)
methods: rct oa; os oa; int oa; rct rlearner; os rlearner; int rlearner; rct rf; os rf; KPS lasso; KPS linear; naive rlearner
benchmark_gap_or_overrides: Preset is J=9, b=2.5; J=1 via eight zero modifiers, b=0 via confounding strength 0. The benchmark draws fixed-size RCT roles, so choose n_rct_train (e.g. 244).
benchmark_method_mapping: int rlearner -> integrative_r_quadratic; other columns have no matching recipe
notes: 1) The expected RCT size is 243.7 (SD 15.6) under the selection model; the text says around 200. 2) README p0 suggestions (1 or p-2) give J=8 or J=1; J=9 needs p0=0. The code comment calls p0 the number of non-zero coefficients, but the code uses it as the number of zero coefficients. 3) The README example (J=8, b=2.5, seed 0, one replicate) prints RMSE 0.866 int, 1.559 rct, 1.457 os, 1.303 naive; it is a different setting from Table 2. 4) The J=1, b=2.5 os rlearner standard-error line prints '1.33(0.01)', duplicating the value printed above it. 5) RCT-only columns are printed once per J and apply to both b. 6) The test set includes the units used for fitting. 7) In R 4.3.3 the README example reproduces its printed RMSEs to seven decimals. A replay of the released code over 100 seeds (replay_intr_tables) agrees with 11 of the 14 R-learner values. The three that differ are in the J=9 rows and are higher in the replay: rct rlearner 1.76 against 1.64, and at b=0 os rlearner 1.07 against 0.97 and naive rlearner 0.82 against 0.77. The replay's RCT size averages 242.8 (SD 14.0). The benchmark translation agrees with the released code in all four cells.
